correctness.rationale: For exposed dual circular arcs of an extremal unit-diameter set in R³, the original Bogosel Proposition11 supplies actual exposed dual-incidence replacement and +2 diametral pairs under each interior dangling insertion. The dual arc is a circle radius rho=√(1−s²/4) with minor angle phi<pi; chord subarc f_L(t)=2rho sin(t/2), spherical-distance subarc f_theta(t)=2asin(rho sin(t/2)). Only the original dual pair contribution changes, giving the exact additive subdivision identity for both q=L,theta. Differentiation yields f_L″=−(rho/2)sin(t/2) and f_theta″=−rho(1−rho²)sin(t/2)/(2(1−rho² sin²(t/2))^{3/2}), strictly negative since s>0. Jensen proves unique equal-angle finite r optimum and f(t)/t strictly decreasing yields increasing positive gain. Cubic expansions give the stated sharp positive r^{-2} coefficients with O(r^{-4}). Any finite extremal configuration has an exposed dual pair and strict midpoint insertion increases each J_q, so no finite maximizer; Bogosel Theorem15 bounds global J_theta, and L≤theta bounds J_L. Source symbolic verifier fully read and own numerical monotonic gains for s=0.5,1 checked; universal claim comes from geometric lemma plus calculus.
residual_risks: The exposed condition is essential; arbitrary four-endpoint unit patterns are insufficient. No bound on rate uniform under degenerate arcs.

value.rationale: The distinction between a finite configuration maximum and a bounded supremum is structural in the constant-width dual-product extremal problem. Explicit optimal placements for every finite subdivision budget and sharp inverse-square discretization rates are useful for rigorous approximations and rule out finite maximizers, independently of the unknown global supremum value.

limitations: Requires exposed minor dual arcs on actual extremal 3D unit-diameter sets; no arbitrary point moves.
